primitives.name: Learnable Relative Spatial Rotary Position Embedding
primitives.verbatim_quote: - STRPE (learnable spatio-temporal rotary position embedding): q_i = R_{Φ(x_i,y_i)}W_q e_i, k_j = R_{Φ(x_j,y_j)}W_k e_j, v_j = W_v e_j; Φ(x,y) = W_Φ(x‖y); θ_k = 10000^{-2k/d}.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'R_{\\Phi(x_i,y_i)}': 'rotation matrix parameterized by spatial coordinates', 'W_q, W_k, W_v': 'learnable projection matrices', 'e_i': 'embedded point representation', 'x_i, y_i': 'normalized spatial coordinates (dimensionless)', 'd': 'embedding dimension'}
primitives.assumptions: Relative spatial displacement captures interpoint relationships independent of absolute location; attention weights depend only on relative offsets.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When spatial coordinates exceed learned range or when POI semantics vary drastically between domains.

primitives.name: Masking-and-Recovery Task Unification
primitives.verbatim_quote: **Masking-and-recovery scheme** (task transferability): (1) modality masking — mask spatial or temporal modality of a point, recover at same step; (2) sub-trajectory masking — replace ⟨p_s,...,p_e⟩ with mask point p_[m], append start token p_[s], recover autoregressively.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'L': 'total loss function (unitless)', 'x_i, \\hat{x}_i': 'true and predicted spatial coordinates (meters)', 't_i, \\hat{t}_i': 'true and predicted temporal features (seconds)', 'r, \\hat{r}': 'binary end-token indicators (0 or 1)'}
primitives.assumptions: All downstream tasks can be formulated as masked recovery problems; no task-specific head required post-pretraining.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When input data lacks sufficient structure or masking strategy fails to preserve semantic meaning.

layer2.mapping: Enables zero-shot adaptation across diverse tasks by treating them as distinct masking strategies applied to shared encoder.
layer2.telemetry: Downstream task performance after freezing pre-trained model.

primitives.verbatim_quote: - Modality mixing: e_i = MeanPool(TransEnc(⟨e^s_i, e^t_i, e^p_i⟩)) (1-layer Transformer).

primitives.assumptions: Each modality contributes independently to global context; transformer fusion preserves modality-specific information.
primitives.breakdown_regime: If modality embeddings are poorly aligned or inconsistent across datasets.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core innovation lies in the unification of trajectory tasks through masking-recovery paradigms. Each downstream task—such as trajectory prediction, time-to-event estimation, or imputation—is encoded as a specific masking pattern applied to the input sequence. This allows a single frozen model to perform multiple functions without retraining. The STRPE mechanism ensures that spatial attention remains region-invariant by encoding relative displacements rather than absolute positions. Mathematically, this corresponds to a transformation where attention weights depend only on differences in spatial coordinates, i.e., $\mathbf{q}_i^\top \cdot \mathbf{k}_j$ becomes dependent on $\Phi(x_i,y_i) - \Phi(x_j,y_j)$ instead of individual $x_i, y_i$. This enables cross-domain transferability because the model learns spatial relations invariant to coordinate systems. The masking scheme introduces a kernel of flexibility: masking spatial features leads to trajectory prediction, masking temporal features to time estimation, etc. These mappings form an isomorphic set of operations over the same latent space. Failure modes include degradation when POI semantics differ significantly between regions or when the masking strategy does not adequately represent task complexity. The model assumes that all relevant information is encoded in the trajectory triplets (spatial, temporal, POI), which must hold true for both training and deployment domains.
